records.title: No Personal Data in Grocery Pricing Act
records.latest_action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
records.committee: House Committee on Energy and Commerce
old_dashboard_summary_bullets: A covered operator may not use individualized pricing, dynamic pricing, or facial recognition or other biometric data to set item prices.
Enforcement is through the Federal Trade Commission; state attorneys general can bring actions under the bill's requirements.
The bill defines covered operators/stores and pricing/data terms; the provisions would take effect one year after enactment.
records.verified_plain_english_summary: The introduced bill would prohibit covered food-store operators and online platforms from using individualized pricing, biometric/facial-recognition data to set prices, or dynamic pricing. It includes specified permitted practices (including coupons, voluntary loyalty discounts, certain publicly disclosed discounts, markdowns and disclosed service fees), provides FTC enforcement, authorizes qualifying state attorneys general to bring civil actions, preserves stronger state-law protections, and takes effect one year after enactment.
